# What 1Password service account tokens the library redacts, and what it leaves
# alone.
#
# A token is the prefix ops_ and, behind it, the account's credentials
# serialized into a JSON object and written out in base64url. The three
# characters that encoding opens with are the same in every token: a JSON object
# begins with a brace and a quoted key, and base64 spells those two bytes and
# the top two bits of the third as eyJ. So ops_eyJ is what a token is located
# by, and it holds whichever key 1Password writes first.
#
# Every token below is written that way and then finished with the ordered run
# 0123456789abcdef, which no real credential is. What the run stands in for is
# the master unlock key, the Secret Key, the SRP verifier and the addresses a
# real token carries six hundred or so characters of; the pattern reads them as
# a run against a floor rather than to a count, so a hundred and sixty
# characters state the same grammar.
#
# The two cases under the over-match heading carry no ordered run at all. They
# are not tokens and nobody issued them: what they hold is a blob that opens the
# way a token does, which is the whole of what the pattern asks for.

patterns: 1password-service-account-token

# The places a token is written. 1Password's CLI reads one out of
# OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN, which is where a token stands in a pipeline and in
# the file a pipeline is configured from.

case:     a token in the environment variable the CLI reads
in:       OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN=ops_eyJ0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abc
out:      OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN=«1password-service-account-token»

case:     a token on a command line
in:       OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN=ops_eyJ0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abc op item get login
out:      OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN=«1password-service-account-token» op item get login

case:     a token in a workflow secret
in:       {"secrets":{"OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN":"ops_eyJ0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abc"}}
out:      {"secrets":{"OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN":"«1password-service-account-token»"}}

# The alphabet the body is written in. 1Password states the encoding as
# base64url, so the letters of both cases, the digits, the hyphen and the
# underscore. The two characters standard base64 writes in place of the last
# two, the plus and the slash, are not admitted — and because the body is read
# to the end of its run, a character outside the alphabet standing inside a
# token leaves what is in front of it short of the floor rather than leaving a
# shorter token.

case:     a body carrying a hyphen and an underscore
in:       ops_eyJ0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef012
out:      «1password-service-account-token»

case:     a plus inside the body
in:       ops_eyJ0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef+0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      ops_eyJ0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef+0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a slash inside the body
in:       ops_eyJ0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef/0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      ops_eyJ0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef/0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a dot inside the body
in:       ops_eyJ0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      ops_eyJ0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

# How long a body is, which the pattern reads as a floor and not as a count. The
# object carries an email address and a sign-in address, both as long as the
# account made them, so no token has a length to read. The floor is a hundred
# and sixty characters, the base64url length of the smallest object that can
# carry both of the secrets a token is a credential by, and the two cases below
# stand at it and one character short of it. What the lower one costs is on the
# record: a line cut to a column limit comes through, and a token is long enough
# that this is the ordinary way to meet half of one.

case:     a body exactly as long as the floor
in:       ops_eyJ0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abc
out:      «1password-service-account-token»

case:     a body one character short of the floor
in:       ops_eyJ0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab
out:      ops_eyJ0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab

# What a token may be written against, and what it draws in. The anchor is the
# whole of what a token is found by and there is no boundary on either side of
# it, so a token keeps its span whatever word character stands in front of it.
# Behind it the redaction reaches to the end of the run, which is the price of
# reading a run rather than a count: a character of the token's own alphabet
# written straight after a token is redacted with the token, and a space, a dot
# or a quote is not.

case:     a token after an underscore
in:       OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN_ops_eyJ0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abc
out:      OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN_«1password-service-account-token»

case:     a token after a letter
in:       xops_eyJ0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abc
out:      x«1password-service-account-token»

case:     a token at the end of a sentence
in:       the token is ops_eyJ0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abc.
out:      the token is «1password-service-account-token».

case:     a token inside quotes
in:       export OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN="ops_eyJ0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abc"
out:      export OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN="«1password-service-account-token»"

case:     a token before a hyphenated word
in:       ops_eyJ0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abc-suffix
out:      «1password-service-account-token»

case:     a token before a word
in:       ops_eyJ0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcsuffix
out:      «1password-service-account-token»

# Two tokens written together. Every character of the anchor belongs to the
# alphabet a body is, the underscore included, so a token can begin inside the
# span of the one before it; the two spans overlap and are redacted as one.
# Written apart, both go.

case:     a token beginning inside the token before it
in:       ops_eyJops_eyJ0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abc
out:      «1password-service-account-token»

case:     two tokens separated by a space
in:       ops_eyJ0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abc ops_eyJ0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef012
out:      «1password-service-account-token» «1password-service-account-token»

# What this pattern redacts that nobody issued. The anchor is seven characters
# of the base64url alphabet, so a long enough encoding written in that alphabet
# carries them somewhere, and everything from there to the end of the encoding
# is redacted. What is taken there is a stretch of a value already opaque to a
# reader, and one of the seven characters is the underscore, which standard
# base64 never writes — so a certificate, a PEM body or an embedded image holds
# no anchor at however long it runs.

case:     the anchor inside a longer run of the alphabet
in:       payload=zzzzops_eyJzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzz
out:      payload=zzzz«1password-service-account-token»

case:     the anchor where a signature stands
in:       eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.zzzzops_eyJzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzz
out:      eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.zzzz«1password-service-account-token»

# And what this pattern leaves alone. The first three are the three characters
# the encoding opens with: read in the case base64 writes them, read in all
# three, and asked for at all. The three after them are the prefix, read in its
# own case, in all four of its characters, and asked for against the header
# rather than apart from it. The one after those turns the pair around and
# writes the header with no prefix in front of it, so that neither half is read
# as a token on its own. Of the last three, a JWT behind the prefix closes its
# header segment on a dot twenty characters in, which no body is written with;
# the names carrying ops_ are what a line about an operations repository is full
# of, and the header is the whole of what turns them away; and a digest carries
# no underscore for the prefix and neither a y nor a J for the header.

case:     a header in the wrong case
in:       ops_EYJ0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abc
out:      ops_EYJ0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abc

case:     two characters of the header
in:       ops_ey0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd
out:      ops_ey0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd

case:     a body carrying no header at all
in:       ops_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      ops_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     an uppercase prefix
in:       OPS_eyJ0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abc
out:      OPS_eyJ0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abc

case:     a hyphen where the prefix carries an underscore
in:       ops-eyJ0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abc
out:      ops-eyJ0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abc

case:     a space between the prefix and the header
in:       ops_ eyJ0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abc
out:      ops_ eyJ0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abc

case:     the header with no prefix in front of it
in:       eyJ0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abc
out:      eyJ0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abc

case:     a jwt behind the prefix
in:       ops_eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      ops_eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef

case:     names carrying the prefix
in:       the ops_team runbook lives beside ops_runbook and ops_oncall
out:      the ops_team runbook lives beside ops_runbook and ops_oncall

case:     a git sha
in:       0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
